In this video, we go through a variety of ice cream stabilizers and how to combine them to make the perfect combination. There are a lot of ice cream stabilizers, some of which can be combined to make a SUPER ice cream stabiizer blend. 
The perfect ice cream stabilizer does exist and you can find yours by adapting 2 or even 4 diferent stabilizers and emulsifiers to make the perfect combination. 
If you want to get involved with these, jump on in and see what its all about.

⁠​⁠ @hasan1980hb there are several reasons one might want to make a low fat ice cream or other low fat frozen desserts. 

- digestion issues with high fat foods
- sorbets are essentially zero fat and thus benefit from stabilizers to obtain ice cream like textures
- calorie reduction 
— fats are the most calorie dense macronutrient, so reducing fat can allow for someone to enjoy ice cream more regularly without going over their caloric needs.
— many higher protein ice creams try to keep fat to a minimum to focus on protein levels (essentially a way of taking in protein other than a typical protein shake)
- curiosity, one might simply be interested in food science and want to understand how stabilizers effect textures in different applications including high fat and low fat recipes.

You are absolutely right that blindly preferring “low fat” can often be a trap since many foods at the store that are marketed as “low fat” have a bunch of sugar packed it to make them more palatable; however, in this context we are discussing home made ice creams, so we can control everything about it, including the sugars.
